problemStatement.formal: v \perp w \Longrightarrow \lVert v + w \rVert^2 = \lVert v \rVert^2 + \lVert w \rVert^2
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the Pythagorean theorem for perpendicular vectors in a two-dimensional Euclidean model, together with the converse and standard numerical triples.
whyMatters: This is a compact test case for Euclidean geometry, norms, inner products, and perpendicularity.
The theorem is the base identity behind distance formulas and many later geometric formalizations.

proven: `norm_sq_eq_inner` connects the vector norm square to the inner product.
`perp_symm` proves symmetry of the perpendicular relation.
`pythagorean_theorem` proves the main norm-square identity for perpendicular vectors.
`pythagorean_converse` proves the converse direction from the norm identity to perpendicularity.
`pythagorean_sum` generalizes the identity to finite mutually perpendicular vector families.
knownResults.goal: Use the completed two-dimensional vector proof as a stable geometry example and reference point for richer Euclidean developments.
